name: Avoid Feature Creep
summary: Keeps a change scoped to what was asked. Flags extra features, refactors, and 'while we are here' edits, and moves them to a suggestions list instead of the diff. Use when a request is small and the agent is about to expand it, when a PRD grows beyond its problem statement, or when the user says 'just do what I asked'.

name: Convex
summary: convex — an installable skill for AI agents.

name: Convex Agents
summary: Building AI agents with the Convex Agent component including thread management, tool integration, streaming responses, RAG patterns, and workflow orchestration

name: Convex Best Practices
summary: Guidelines for building production-ready Convex apps covering function organization, query patterns, validation, TypeScript usage, error handling, and the Zen of Convex design philosophy

name: Convex Component Authoring
summary: Creates reusable Convex components with defineComponent, a clean client wrapper, their own schema, and an npm publish setup. Use when extracting a feature into a package, building something for the Convex component directory, or when a component's functions are not showing up in the parent app.

name: Convex Cron Jobs
summary: Scheduled function patterns for background tasks including interval scheduling, cron expressions, job monitoring, retry strategies, and best practices for long-running tasks

name: Convex File Storage
summary: Complete file handling including upload flows, serving files via URL, storing generated files from actions, deletion, and accessing file metadata from system tables

name: Convex Functions
summary: Writes Convex queries, mutations, actions, and internal functions in the object form with args and returns validators, correct ctx usage, runtime boundaries, and error handling. Use when adding or changing anything in convex/*.ts that exports a function, or when deciding between query, mutation, and action.

name: Convex Http Actions
summary: External API integration and webhook handling including HTTP endpoint routing, request/response handling, authentication, CORS configuration, and webhook signature validation

name: Convex Migrations
summary: Schema migration strategies for evolving applications including adding new fields, backfilling data, removing deprecated fields, index migrations, and zero-downtime migration patterns

name: Convex Realtime
summary: Patterns for building reactive apps including subscription management, optimistic updates, cache behavior, and paginated queries with cursor-based loading

name: Convex Schema Validator
summary: Designs convex/schema.ts tables, validators, indexes, and relationships, and keeps the schema honest as data evolves. Use when creating tables, adding fields, choosing index fields, modeling relationships, or when a validator error appears at deploy time.

name: Convex Security Audit
summary: Deep security review patterns for authorization logic, data access boundaries, action isolation, rate limiting, and protecting sensitive operations

name: Convex Security Check
summary: Quick security audit checklist covering authentication, function exposure, argument validation, row-level access control, and environment variable handling
